title: A layer can say how it mixes with what is under it
goal: A layer today always paints straight over what is below it. Give every layer a way to say how it mixes instead - multiply to burn a colour into the content beneath, screen to lighten it, and the few others that earn their place - so a tint over a screenshot, a highlighter mark over text, or a darkened region is one setting rather than a trick. It sits with the layer's opacity, because it answers the same question: how much of what is under this shows through.
notes:
Asked for by the user on 2026-09-09: they raised Photoshop's layer mixing modes as the powerful-but-unintuitive prior art and asked whether Photonz should have them.

Worth being straight about in the build: a blend mode CANNOT blur or pixelate. Those are neighbourhood operations that read surrounding pixels; a blend mode is per-pixel maths between this layer's colour and the backdrop's. Photoshop does blur-through-a-shape with a smart filter or a blurred duplicate, not with a blend mode. So this task is the tinting and burning axis only; blur, pixelate, greyscale and invert belong to the sibling task 'A layer can change what is underneath it', which is the other axis. Neither replaces the other.

Most of this already exists and is not exposed. BlendMode is in Sources/PhotonzCore/Layer.swift:931 with normal, multiply and screen; LayerStyle carries it (Layer.swift:964); DocumentRenderer.swift:478 composites with it and DocumentRenderer.swift:1307 maps it to CIMultiplyBlendMode and CIScreenBlendMode. Nothing in Sources/Photonz puts it in front of a person - grep for blendMode in the app layer finds only the drag preview. So the work is mostly the model round-trip, the panel row, and deciding which modes earn a place.

Which modes: resist shipping Photoshop's full list. Start from what a redline or a screenshot markup actually needs - multiply (burn a colour in, highlighter), screen (lighten), and consider darken, lighten and overlay - and justify each addition in the audit. A list of twenty with names like 'linear burn' is precisely the unintuitive thing the user objected to.

Not confirmed: whether the group buffering path composites a child's blend mode against the group's own buffer or against the canvas. DocumentRenderer.swift:430 has a pass-through fast path for a plain group that composites children straight onto the output, which likely means a multiply child inside such a group already mixes with the whole canvas. Reproduce that before deciding what correct means, and write the test for it first.

Check Sources/Photonz/Releases/ before assuming one shared change reaches both releases; per CLAUDE.md a Current change is not finished until Next has it.
acceptance: Every layer has a mix setting in the panel, next to opacity, with plain names and a live preview as you move through the list
Multiply and screen work and are pixel-tested against a known backdrop; any further modes added are pixel-tested the same way
The names are in plain language and each one says what it does in its tooltip, so a person who has never used Photoshop can pick the right one
The setting round-trips through save and load, survives duplicate, group and ungroup, and undoes
It composites correctly inside a group: a layer set to multiply inside a group mixes with the group's contents, not with the whole canvas behind the group
Export and copy carry the mix, checked by sampling exported pixels
Audit under queue/audits/ showing each mode over the same backdrop, and anything rough filed as a follow-up
